summary:
ASTRA VITALIS: Astronaut Health Intelligence System

ASTRA VITALIS is a research prototype developed to explore astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. It features an interactive dashboard for monitoring cardiovascular activity, sleep, physical activity, stress and blood oxygen levels. An Isolation Forest machine-learning model identifies unusual patterns in simulated crew-health data, helping highlight records that may require further review.

The project also incorporates real NASA OSD-575 Inspiration4 blood serum data to analyse glucose, albumin, creatinine and sodium levels against their recorded reference ranges. This adds a research-based perspective to the monitoring system.

ASTRA VITALIS addresses the challenge of supporting astronaut health awareness when continuous observation and timely identification of unusual patterns are important. By combining data visualization, machine learning and publicly available spaceflight research, it demonstrates how digital tools could support health monitoring and research for future long-duration missions.
details:
ASTRA VITALIS is an astronaut health monitoring research prototype that brings health tracking, anomaly detection and NASA research data into one interactive dashboard for long-duration space missions.

What it does: A Streamlit dashboard lets users select a crew member and mission day to view heart rate, sleep, activity, stress and SpO2 (simulated data). An Isolation Forest model (150 estimators, contamination 0.12) flags unusual combinations of these indicators for human review. A NASA Research Archive explores real Inspiration4 blood serum data (NASA OSD-575): 28 samples, 4 participants, 7 timepoints and 4 parameters (glucose, albumin, creatinine, sodium). Of 112 comparisons against the dataset's reference ranges, 104 were within range, 5 below and 3 above.

Impact: It gives mission teams one clearer view of crew health signals and surfaces unusual patterns for review. All flags are research flags, not medical diagnoses.

Tools: Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, Plotly, Scikit-learn, Jupyter Notebook.

Creativity and limitations: It combines simulated monitoring data with real NASA data in separate modules and states its limits clearly. The model is not clinically validated. Next steps: real wearable data, persistent crew records and validated models.
dataRefs: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) – Inspiration4 Mission, OSD-575 Blood Serum Analysis Dataset
